entities.summary: Albert of Pisa, O.Min., was a prominent Italian Franciscan friar who played a pivotal role in the spiritual and administrative landscape of the 13th century. Born in Pisa, Italy, and ordained as a friar in 1220, he quickly rose through the ranks of the Franciscan Order, becoming the Minister General in 1239. This election marked a significant turning point in the order's history, as it signaled a shift towards greater centralization and standardization. As Minister General, Albert of Pisa oversaw the reform of the Franciscan Order's rules and practices, introducing new devotional practices and emphasizing the importance of preaching and evangelism. He also played a key role in the Second Lateran Council, which took place in 1245 and addressed issues of clerical corruption, heresy, and the role of the papacy. Albert's leadership during this period helped to establish the Franciscan Order as a major force in European spirituality and politics. His legacy extends beyond the realm of the Franciscans, however, as he also played a role in shaping the broader intellectual and cultural landscape of the Middle Ages. The influence of Albert of Pisa can be seen in the development of Scholasticism, which emphasized the use of reason and scriptural interpretation to understand Christian doctrine. His commitment to the principles of poverty, simplicity, and evangelism also resonated with the emerging movements of spiritual reform and mysticism. In the centuries that followed, Albert of Pisa's example would inspire countless generations of theologians, mystics, and reformers, cementing his place as one of the most significant figures of the Middle Ages.
